story_type: frozen football smashed to show spacecraft launch and cold tests
hook: NASA froze a football in liquid nitrogen. Then it got the hammer.
narration: NASA froze a football in liquid nitrogen, then hit it with a hammer.
It was a demo by the engineers building the James Webb Space Telescope.
A field goal kick hits a football with a little more than four Gs.
During launch, parts of Webb could feel up to nineteen Gs, nineteen times their own weight.
So every part gets shaken, spun in a centrifuge, and blasted with rocket level sound in a giant acoustic chamber.
Then the cold. Webb's instruments have to work very near absolute zero, minus four hundred fifty nine degrees Fahrenheit.
Liquid nitrogen is still warmer than some of those instruments.
[short pause] Then the hammer came down.
outcome: The rubber bladder inside shattered, but the outer shell held together.
title: NASA froze a football, then smashed it
description:
Engineers at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, put a football through versions of the launch and cold tests used on the James Webb Space Telescope, ending with a soak in liquid nitrogen and a hammer.
